newsitem.title: UK: UK officials get access to nurses held in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: UK officials get access to nurses held in Saudi.

text.p: Britain and Saudi Arabia pulled back from a diplomatic confrontation on Tuesday when British embassy officials were told they could visit two nurses held for four days in Dhahran on a murder charge.

The Foreign Office said Saudi authorities had finally agreed to a request by local embassy staff to visit the two women, who have been held since Friday. The agreement follows 48 hours of intense diplomatic pressure.
The two are being questioned about the murder of an Australian nurse at a military hospital. Previous attempts by the British consul to gain access to them had failed.
Saudi authorities are reported to have confiscated the passports of another 40 British nationals in connection with the murder investigation.
The Foreign Office said embassy officials expected to visit the two nurses later on Tuesday. They also hoped to establish whether they have been formally charged.
The two women, who have not been named, are being questioned about the murder of 55-year-old Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford, at the King Fahd Military Medical Complex in Dhahran.
Gilford's body was found in her room on December 11. She had been stabbed four times, battered with a hammer and smothered.
Human rights groups have expressed concern over the detention of the two women, who could face public beheading if they are convicted of murder.
